title: AI-based Intrusion Detection System alert and emergency braking avert Kamrup Express collision with about 60 elephants in Assam
summary: 16 October 2024: AI intrusion alert and crew braking stopped 15959 Kamrup Express as about 60 elephants crossed near Lamsakhang, Assam
account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 pm, train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. NFR reported it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024.
purpose: Built to detect elephants near the track and alert loco pilots, station masters and control rooms. This benefit is that purpose.
system: AI-based Intrusion Detection System (distributed acoustic sensing on optical fiber), Northeast Frontier Railway
taxonomy_note: The collision avoided is between a train and elephants, so the gain is shared with conservation.

ratings.reason: NFR avoided a collision between a running express train and about 60 elephants, with the derailment and disruption risk that carries.
About 60 wild elephants, a protected species, crossed safely; NFR reports hundreds of such events a year on this network.

ai_role.statement: The operator's release says the drivers noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake and were “also alerted” by the IDS. One local report says the braking followed the IDS warning. The AI alert is documented, but its share of the causal credit is not separable from the crew's own sighting. Hence protective response, prevention unproven.

fields.account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 pm, train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. NFR reported it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024.

NFR reported it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024.
